title: AI-generated hiring language can convert recruiting automation into an enforceable exclusion and institutional correction
source_unit: US Department of Justice Immigrant and Employee Rights Section investigation and settlement record
geography: United States; Elegant Enterprise-Wide Solutions, Inc., a Virginia-based IT services provider

denominator.unit: AI-generated job advertisements identified in the DOJ settlement summary

automated_surface.value: job advertisements generated by an artificial-intelligence tool

exclusion_rule.value: advertisements restricted certain positions by citizenship status, including consideration only of H-1B, OPT, or H-4 visa holders, without legal justification
exclusion_rule.unit: alleged discriminatory recruiting language resolved by settlement

institutional_response.value: DOJ IER settlement; $9,460 civil penalty, employee training, and prohibition on future unlawful exclusion

worker_specific_recovery.value: no back-pay or applicant-level receipt reported on the public summary

observations.method: Targeted review of the official DOJ Civil Rights Division settlement press release and settlements ledger; no applicant file or settlement attachment downloaded.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary identifies the employer, tool-generated advertisements, legal issue, and institutional remedy, but does not disclose the number of affected applicants, whether any applicant was denied a particular job, tool configuration, ad reach, payment to an individual, later compliance, or subsequent applicant behavior.
observations.subgroup: US workers and job applicants affected by the named employer's recruitment advertisements; the public record does not provide a complete applicant denominator or subgroup table.
observations.counterinterpretation: The settlement shows that AI-generated language can participate in an unlawful hiring process, but it does not show that the tool independently made a hiring decision or that every AI-assisted advertisement was discriminatory. A civil penalty and training requirement are institutional correction, not proof of restored opportunity or durable compliance.

observations.period: 2026-02-23 executed settlement agreement; three-year term from latest signature

denominator.unit: redacted charging-party investigation; public agreement also identifies two discriminatory advertisements

charge_and_investigation.value: IER accepted a complete charge on 2025-12-01, opened an investigation on 2025-12-02, and found reasonable cause to believe discriminatory advertisements were posted

agreement_duration.value: three years following the effective date

prospective_controls.value: bilingual worker-rights posters, policy review/revision within 60 days, paid compliance training within 60 days, attendance records, and IER compliance inquiries

enforcement_loop.value: IER may request reports, inspect premises, interview personnel, and allow 30 days to cure a suspected violation before pursuing further enforcement

individual_recovery.value: no back pay or restored job consideration specified; individuals retain the right to file a charge

observations.method: Targeted review of the redacted five-page official DOJ settlement agreement linked from the public settlements ledger; PDF retrieved for page-level inspection and hashed, but not retained in Git.
observations.uncertainty: The charging party and affected positions are redacted. The agreement does not disclose ad reach, applicant count, individual denial, whether the AI tool generated the restriction or received it from a human, completion of each control, or any later compliance finding.
observations.subgroup: One redacted charging party and potentially other applicants; the public agreement provides no complete affected-person denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A three-year monitoring and cure architecture is stronger than a one-time penalty, but a contractual right to inquire or file a charge is not proof that monitoring occurred, a violation was cured, or an applicant recovered an opportunity.

related_sources.claim: The DOJ settlement ledger identifies Elegant's February 2026 settlement terms and places it within the broader Protecting U.S. Workers enforcement series.
A 2026-09-17 official-source recheck found no public payment confirmation, monitoring/cure result, or applicant-level restoration record; this is a bounded non-observation.
The worker/workplace ledger defines the missing exposure, outcome, voice, household, and exit fields.

boundary: This is a named US AI-assisted recruiting enforcement event linking automated language to an alleged exclusion and dated institutional correction. It does not estimate AI discrimination prevalence, independently identify the model's role in the decision, establish applicant-level opportunity loss or recovery, or close later trust, switching, political action, household, or geopolitical consequences.
